problems.title: Affine composition does not preserve gradient paths
problems.source_location: Theorem 4.1(2), PDF p.4; Proposition 4.2 and discussion, p.5; Appendix A.2, Eqs.(10)–(12), p.24
claim: The paper claims equivalence in parameter space and gradient-update paths between factorized prompt/classifier optimization and direct affine optimization.
analysis: Use scalar \(z=w(ah+b)\), squared loss \(z^2/2\), and \(h=1,a=w=1,b=0\). All three factor gradients equal \(1\), so a step \(\eta=1/10\) gives \(a_+=w_+=0.9,b_+=-0.1\) and prediction \(0.72\). The direct affine model \(vh+c\), initialized at the identical function \((v,c)=(1,0)\), instead gives \((0.9,-0.1)\) and prediction \(0.8\). Initial effective directions \((-2,-1)\) and \((-1,-1)\) are not proportional. Generally, for \(B=AS\) and \(G=\nabla_B L\), the exact factor update is \[B_+=B-\eta(GS^\top S+AA^\top G)+\eta^2GS^\top A^\top G.\]
result: The central gradient-path equivalence is false, even at the favorable scalar orthogonality initialization in the appendix. Forward functional composition remains correct.
repair: Retain the forward affine identity and state the induced factor-optimization dynamics, rather than Euclidean gradient equivalence.
problems.impact_rationale: Exact one-step and infinitesimal counterexamples refute the main mechanism theorem identifying prompting with linear probing.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Reverse affine correspondence requires sufficient rank
problems.source_location: Definition 4.1, PDF p.4; Appendix A.2, Eq.(9), p.24
claim: The proof maps arbitrary affine classifier parameters back to factorized parameters without a stated width restriction, and describes a unique mapping.
analysis: Every augmented coefficient matrix \(B=AS\) has rank at most the prompt width \(d_{\rm p}\). For \(d=k=2,d_{\rm p}=1\), the identity classifier has augmented matrix \([I_2\ 0]\) of rank \(2\), impossible for those factors. Even at sufficient width, \(AS=(AQ^{-1})(QS)\) for every invertible \(Q\), so the factorization is generally nonunique.
result: The unrestricted reverse parameter-space equivalence fails. The one-way functional proposition is valid, and a chosen inverse after fixing additional factors is a narrower notion than a unique reparameterization.
repair: The representable affine maps are exactly those with augmented rank at most \(d_{\rm p}\); all maps are covered when \(d_{\rm p}\geq\min(k,d+1)\). State the nonuniqueness explicitly.
problems.impact_rationale: The rank obstruction independently invalidates unrestricted parameter-space equivalence underlying the main theorem.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Detached embeddings prevent supervised prompt gradients
problems.source_location: Section 5, PDF pp.5–6; main.py, lines 130–168; model/DGI.py, lines 121–125; model/GRACE.py, lines 42–45
claim: The method jointly trains prompt and classifier through a frozen encoder. DGI and GRACE return detached embeddings on that training path.
analysis: The supervised prompt derivative should contain \((D_\Psi H)^\top D_H L\). Detachment removes that route while classifier gradients still exist. Including prompt parameters in Adam cannot supply the missing task derivative. Freezing encoder parameter weights does not require severing derivatives with respect to its input graph. Recursive graph fusion can still change forward values without supervised prompt updates.
result: These two released branches do not implement the described label-driven adaptation. GraphMAE returns nondetached embeddings, so the defect is not universal across backbones. Published score effects and exact historical code remain unknown.
repair: Return differentiable embeddings during adaptation while freezing encoder weights through parameter settings or optimizer exclusion.
problems.impact_rationale: The release blocks the intended prompt gradient in two branches, without establishing their contribution to the published benchmarks.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Early stopping does not restore the monitored graph and model
problems.source_location: Appendix B.1, PDF p.24; main.py, lines 172–200
claim: The driver assigns state dictionaries as best states and restores them while retaining the current recursively fused graph.
analysis: A state dictionary holds tensors sharing live parameter storage: a value saved at \(1\) and later updated to \(2\) remains \(2\) in the un-cloned snapshot. Separately, with \(A_0=0,\tau=1/2,P_1=1,P_2=2\), fused graph states are \(A_1=1/2,A_2=5/4\). Restoring first-epoch parameters while keeping \(A_2\) cannot recreate the monitored first-epoch input.
result: The checkpoint procedure does not generally recover the best-loss evaluation state. The sign and magnitude of benchmark bias are unknown; a final-best epoch can make the mismatch immaterial.
repair: Clone prompt/classifier states and fused edge indices/weights at the monitored forward state, and restore that complete tuple for evaluation.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a released checkpoint-selection defect; no corrected performance ordering or systematic bias is established.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

impact_rationale: Major: the central parameter-space and gradient-path equivalence fails by exact scalar and rank counterexamples.
